newsitem.title: FRANCE: RUGBY UNION-VILLEPREUX HOLDS FIRST FRANCE PRACTICE.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-VILLEPREUX HOLDS FIRST FRANCE PRACTICE.

text.p: Pierre Villepreux, appointed to help France rediscover their open attacking game, held his first practice on Tuesday ahead of their Five Nations match against Ireland in Dublin on Saturday.
The French team management named Villepreux, who in the 1980s sowed the seeds of Toulouse's current successes, as assistant to coach Jean-Claude Skrela last week.
Former England coach Roger Uttley, who enlisted Villepreux's help for an England training camp ahead of the 1989 Five Nations championship, said Villepreux was man ahead of the times.
"The style he believes in is that which prevails today. He was right before everyone else," Utlley told the French sport daily L'Equipe.
Villepreux's method involves building moves not from a static phase but from situations of apparent disorder, according to some of his former proteges.

Serge Gabernet, a former back and now coach of the France A team, said: "You had to forget the number on your back and, in the movements, each player had to have in mind two or three possibilities to adapt to the situations that developed."
Other former players also said Villepreux always kept them in doubt as to their selection, often telling them they were not the best option in their positions so as to push them to improve.
Former player Jean-Michel Giraud warned: "He will be intransigent and certain guys risk falling from high."
The net result, which Skrela hopes will rub off on the curent France internationals, was demanding, dynamic training sessions that led to extreme enjoyment of the game, and success.

Uttley, looking at the Five Nations prospects, said: "I had England as favourites, just ahead of France. But with him (Villepreux) as trainer I must revise my judgement. I'm sure he can tilt the balance in favour of the French."
